derivations.claim:
In a local chart $y^A$ on $C$, write $E_A=d\Phi_\epsilon(\partial_{y^A})$ and $q_{AB}=g_\epsilon(E_A,E_B)$. The flow coordinates give $[k_\epsilon,E_A]=0$, so torsion freedom yields $
abla_{k_\epsilon}E_A=
abla_{E_A}k_\epsilon$. Metric compatibility then gives $\partial_\lambda q_{AB}=B_{AB}+B_{BA}$, where $B_{AB}=g_\epsilon(
abla_{E_A}k_\epsilon,E_B)$ is evaluated on the screen. The cut is spacelike and transverse, so its tangent plane maps isometrically onto the screen quotient in [F2], and $q^{AB}B_{AB}=	heta_\epsilon$. Differentiating the positive determinant explicitly gives $\partial_\lambda\sqrt{\det q}= rac12\sqrt{\det q}\,q^{AB}\partial_\lambda q_{AB}=	heta_\epsilon\sqrt{\det q}$. At $\epsilon=0$, $B_0=0$ makes $\partial_\lambda q_{0,AB}=0$, so $\mu_{0,\lambda}=dA_0$ for every $\lambda$. Integrate the density identity from $\lambda_0$ to $\lambda$ on any finite slab; joint $C^1$ dependence and compactness of $C$ permit differentiation under this finite integral in $\epsilon$. At $\epsilon=0$, $	heta_0=0$ and $\mu_{0,u}=dA_0$, writing $\delta\mu_\lambda:=\left.\partial_\epsilon\mu_{\epsilon,\lambda}ight|_0$ for the varied area density, we obtain the density identity $\delta\mu_\lambda-\delta\mu_{\lambda_0}=\int_{\lambda_0}^{\lambda}\delta	heta(u,\cdot)\,dA_0\,du$ on $C$. Thus $\partial_\lambda\delta\mu_\lambda=\delta	heta(\lambda,\cdot)\,dA_0$, and differentiating its integral over compact $C$ gives $\delta A'(\lambda)=\int_C\delta	heta(\lambda,y)\,dA_0(y)$.

For fixed $y\in C$, integrate [F1] from $\lambda$ to $R>\lambda$: $\delta\theta(R,y)-\delta\theta(\lambda,y)=-8\pi G_N\int_\lambda^R\delta T_{kk}(v,y)\,dv$. Letting $R\to\infty$ is justified by [F1] and [A2], and the future boundary condition gives $\delta\theta(\lambda,y)=8\pi G_N\int_\lambda^\infty\delta T_{kk}(v,y)\,dv$.
Substitute step 1.2 into the area variation from step 1.1. The resulting absolutely convergent integral is $\delta A'(u)=8\pi G_N\int_C dA_0(y)\int_u^\infty\delta T_{kk}(v,y)\,dv$.

By [A2] and step 2.1, $\int_\lambda^\infty|\delta A'(u)|\,du\le8\pi G_N\int_CdA_0\int_\lambda^\infty(v-\lambda)|\delta T_{kk}(v,y)|\,dv<\infty$. Thus $\delta A(R)$ has a finite limit as $R\to\infty$. Fubini's theorem applies to the absolute first moment in [A2], so integrating step 2.1 from $u=\lambda$ to $\infty$ and reversing the order of integration gives $\delta A_\infty-\delta A(\lambda)=8\pi G_N\int_CdA_0\int_\lambda^\infty\delta T_{kk}(v,y)\bigl(\int_\lambda^vdu\bigr)dv=8\pi G_NM_\lambda$.

Since $G_N>0$, divide the equality in step 3.1 by $4G_N$ to obtain $(\delta A_\infty-\delta A(\lambda))/(4G_N)=2\pi M_\lambda$. This is an identity for the signed first-order stress moment; no positivity or entropy interpretation follows.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
Use natural units $c=\hbar=k_B=1$, metric signature $(-,+,+,+)$, and the
curvature convention
$R(X,Y)Z=\nabla_X\nabla_YZ-\nabla_Y\nabla_XZ-\nabla_{[X,Y]}Z$ with
$\operatorname{Ric}_{bd}=g^{ac}R_{abcd}$. Let $M$ be a fixed Hausdorff,
second-countable, oriented smooth four-manifold. For each dimensionless
$\epsilon$ in an open interval about $0$, supply a smooth Lorentzian metric
$g_\epsilon$ on $M$ with the stated signature and a time orientation (a chosen
future timelike cone). Each $(M,g_\epsilon)$ is globally hyperbolic: it is
strongly causal, meaning every point has arbitrarily small neighborhoods that
each causal curve meets in a connected parameter interval, and each causal
diamond $J^+(p)\cap J^-(q)$ is compact. Here causal curves are piecewise
$C^1$ with consistently future- or past-directed causal tangent, and
$J^\pm(p)$ denote points reachable from or reaching $p$ by such curves.

For each $\epsilon$, let $H_\epsilon\subset M$ be a smooth embedded
three-dimensional submanifold whose induced metric has a one-dimensional
radical at every point. Its smooth nowhere-zero future null generator field
$k_\epsilon$ spans that radical and is affine,
$\nabla^{g_\epsilon}_{k_\epsilon}k_\epsilon=0$. At $p\in H_\epsilon$ define
the screen space $\mathcal S_{\epsilon,p}:=k_\epsilon^\perp/\mathbb R
k_\epsilon$, where $k_\epsilon^\perp$ is taken in $T_pM$. Its positive screen
metric is $\bar g_\epsilon([X],[Y]):=g_\epsilon(X,Y)$, its screen deformation
form is
$$B_\epsilon([X],[Y]):=g_\epsilon(\nabla^{g_\epsilon}_Xk_\epsilon,Y),$$
and its expansion and shear are $\theta_\epsilon:=\operatorname{tr}_{\bar
g_\epsilon}B_\epsilon$ and $\sigma_\epsilon:=B_\epsilon-\frac12\theta_\epsilon
\bar g_\epsilon$, respectively. These are the supplied smooth null-screen
conventions. The word “horizon” below denotes only $H_\epsilon$; no causal- or
event-horizon property is assumed.

Fix a nonempty compact smooth two-manifold $C$ and $\lambda_0\in\mathbb R$.
For each $\epsilon$, supply a smooth map
$$\Phi_\epsilon:[\lambda_0,\infty)\times C\to H_\epsilon$$
such that $\partial_\lambda\Phi_\epsilon=k_\epsilon\circ\Phi_\epsilon$, and
every $\Phi_{\epsilon,\lambda}:C\to H_\epsilon$ is an embedding with spacelike
image. The family supplies a fixed identification of generator labels and
affine normalization across $\epsilon$. With $[\lambda]=L$, this
parameterization gives $[k_\epsilon]=1$ in length coordinates.

Write $q_{\epsilon,\lambda}:=\Phi_{\epsilon,\lambda}^*g_\epsilon$ for the
positive-definite induced metric on $C$, and let $\mu_{\epsilon,\lambda}$ be
its Riemannian area density. On each finite parameter slab, the pulled-back
metric, area density, screen deformation form, expansion, and shear are jointly
$C^1$ in $(\epsilon,\lambda)$ and smooth in $y$; the underlying metric and
embedding family has the corresponding $\epsilon$-regularity and spatial
derivatives needed to define them. Call the reference geometry stationary in
this model when $B_0=0$ along every generator; then $\theta_0=\sigma_0=0$.
Define $\delta\theta:=\left.\partial_\epsilon\theta_\epsilon\right|_0$.

For each $\epsilon$, supply a positive normalized state $\omega_\epsilon$ on
the selected free scalar-field algebra. Its two-point distribution $W_\epsilon$
is a bisolution of the selected Klein–Gordon operator and has the supplied
Hadamard wavefront relation $\mathcal C^+_{g_\epsilon}$: pairs of future-null
covectors related by parallel propagation along a future-directed null
geodesic with common positive scale and opposite sign in the second slot,
including the coincident-point case. Supply a state-independent Hadamard
singular bidistribution
$H_{\mu,\epsilon}$ such that $W_\epsilon-H_{\mu,\epsilon}$ is smooth, and one
fixed local stress prescription across the family,
$$T^{\mathrm{ren},\epsilon}_{ab}(x)=\lim_{x'\to x}D^{\epsilon}_{ab}(x,x')\bigl(W_\epsilon-H_{\mu,\epsilon}\bigr)(x,x')+C_{ab}[g_\epsilon;\mu,\mathbf c](x),$$
where $D^{\epsilon}_{ab}$ is the supplied finite-order bidifferential
operator and $C_{ab}$ the supplied state-independent local curvature
correction with the supplier's fixed positive renormalization scale $\mu$
($[\mu]=L^{-1}$ in these natural units) and finite renormalization conditions
$\mathbf c$. Thus the coincidence limit acts on a smooth difference, not on
the singular distributions separately. The family
$$F_\epsilon(\lambda,y):=(T^{\mathrm{ren},\epsilon}_{ab}k_\epsilon^ak_\epsilon^b)\bigl(\Phi_\epsilon(\lambda,y)\bigr)$$
is jointly $C^1$ in $\epsilon$ and continuous in $(\lambda,y)$ on each finite
parameter slab. No independent graviton-fluctuation source is included.

Restrict every model input to the admissible domain supplied with its chosen
effective-model instance and to the regime below the supplier's positive energy
cutoff $E_{\mathrm{cut}}$. The supplier's SI cutoff is measured in joules; in
the natural units fixed here, $[E_{\mathrm{cut}}]=L^{-1}$. Neither the cutoff
value nor its admissible input domain is chosen here. Keep any prescribed
retarded data as supplied inputs, without
imposing a collapse geometry or scattering history. Select the
Einstein-Hilbert submodel by setting the supplier's curvature-squared couplings
to zero. Write $G_N$ for the supplier's Newton's constant $G$ in the natural-unit
convention $c=\hbar=k_B=1$, so $G_N>0$ has dimension $L^2$. Define
$$\delta T_{kk}(\lambda,y):=\left.\partial_\epsilon F_\epsilon(\lambda,y)\right|_0.$$
Then $[\lambda]=L$, $[k_\epsilon]=1$, $[\delta T_{kk}]=L^{-4}$, and
$[\delta\theta]=L^{-1}$.
Assume $\delta T_{kk}$ is continuous, its tail is absolutely integrable on
each generator, and
$$\int_C dA_0\int_{\lambda_0}^{\infty}(v-\lambda_0)|\delta T_{kk}(v,y)|\,dv<\infty,$$
where $dA_0:=\mu_{0,\lambda_0}$ is the reference background area density.
Adopt, only to first order in $\epsilon$, the linearized focusing equation and
future boundary condition
$$\partial_\lambda\delta\theta(\lambda,y)=-8\pi G_N\delta T_{kk}(\lambda,y),\qquad \lim_{\lambda\to\infty}\delta\theta(\lambda,y)=0.$$
Terms quadratic in expansion or shear are omitted only at this first
perturbative order: both vanish in the stationary reference geometry and are
of order $\epsilon$ in the supplied family, so their squares are of order
$\epsilon^2$.
This postulate is an adopted model equation; it neither asserts that the model
describes nature nor identifies its null-stress moment with modular energy or
entropy.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
Let $(\mathcal M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold of signature $(-,+,+,+)$, with the metric-selected connection $\nabla$ of [[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]. Here $N$ is the supplied smooth future timelike vector field defining the time orientation; it is not a coordinate frame or a tetrad.

A **smooth null hypersurface** is a smooth embedded three-dimensional submanifold $H\subset\mathcal M$ such that, at every $p\in H$, the restriction of $g_p$ to $T_pH$ has a one-dimensional radical
$$L_p:=\{v\in T_pH:g_p(v,w)=0\text{ for every }w\in T_pH\}.$$
Write $i:H\hookrightarrow\mathcal M$ for the inclusion, and let $\pi:T\mathcal M\to\mathcal M$ be the tangent-bundle projection. A smooth vector field $V$ along $H$ means a smooth map $V:H\to T\mathcal M$ with $\pi\circ V=i$, equivalently a smooth section of
$$i^*T\mathcal M=\{(p,v):p\in H,\ v\in T_p\mathcal M\}.$$
For a smooth tangent field $X$ on $H$, the notation $\nabla_XV$ means $(i^*\nabla)_XV$, using the pullback connection of [[def-pullback-connection]] for the ambient metric-selected connection $\nabla$; its prescription in a pulled-back frame and frame-independent well-definedness are given by [[thm-pullback-connection-is-well-defined-and-functorial]]. It agrees with restricting $\nabla_{\widetilde X}\widetilde V$ for any local smooth ambient extensions when $V$ and $X$ are restricted to $H$. Such extensions exist in the slice coordinates of [[def-embedded-submanifold-and-slice-chart]] by extending coordinate coefficients smoothly off the slice. For tangent $X,Y$, extending their tangential coordinate coefficients independently of the transverse coordinate and setting their transverse components to zero makes the ambient bracket restrict to the intrinsic bracket on $H$. Restricting the ambient metric-compatibility and torsion-free identities therefore gives, for tangent $X,Y$ on $H$ and fields $V,W$ along $H$,
$$Xg(V,W)=g(\nabla_XV,W)+g(V,\nabla_XW),\qquad \nabla_XY-\nabla_YX=[X,Y].$$
Pullback functoriality along any integral curve $\gamma$ in $H$ identifies the curve derivative with the pullback of $i^*\nabla$; accordingly $\nabla_k k=0$ means the tangent field is parallel along its generator with this affine parameter.

A **smooth affine null generator field** on $H$ is a smooth vector field $k$ along $H$ such that $k_p$ is a nonzero future-directed section of $L_p$ and $\nabla_k k=0$ along $H$. Thus $k$ is both tangent and normal to $H$, and its integral-curve parameter is affine.

For each $p\in H$, the **screen space** is the quotient vector space
$$\mathcal S_p:=k_p^\perp/\mathbb R k_p,\qquad k_p^\perp:=\{v\in T_p\mathcal M:g_p(v,k_p)=0\}.$$
Its candidate **screen metric** is $\bar g_p([X],[Y]):=g_p(X,Y)$. The result [[lem-tgr-null-screen-quotient-positive]] establishes that these spaces form a smooth rank-two vector bundle over $H$ and that $\bar g$ is a well-defined positive-definite metric on it.

For smooth local screen sections represented by smooth fields $X,Y$ tangent to $H$, define the **screen deformation form**
$$B([X],[Y]):=g(\nabla_X k,Y).$$
The same lemma establishes that this form is well defined on the quotient. Its **expansion** is $\theta:=\operatorname{tr}_{\bar g}B$ and its **shear** is $\sigma:=B-\frac12\theta\bar g$. In the area theorem below, $B$ is proved symmetric, so $\sigma$ is a symmetric trace-free form on each screen space.

Independently, let
$$\mathcal P:=\{(m,a,q)\in\mathbb R^3:m>0,\ m^2>a^2+q^2\}.$$
These are real mathematical parameters with no physical units assigned here. On this open parameter domain set
$$s:=\sqrt{m^2-a^2-q^2},\quad r_+:=m+s,\quad D:=r_+^2+a^2,$$
$$A:=4\pi D,\quad j:=ma,\quad \kappa_{\rm KN}:=\frac{r_+-m}{D},\quad \Omega_{\rm KN}:=\frac{a}{D},\quad \Phi_{\rm KN}:=\frac{qr_+}{D}.$$
Because the radicand and $D$ are strictly positive on $\mathcal P$, these are smooth real-valued functions there: the repeated derivative formula for $x^{1/2}$ on $(0,\infty)$ and the chain rule are given in [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]], Facts [F2]. This definition assigns no geometric or thermodynamic interpretation to these functions and asserts no event-horizon existence, formation, uniqueness or thermodynamic-identification theorem.

risk_review.notes: Independently read all five current proof steps and direct Postulate/screen suppliers including the positive-screen lemma. The cut tangent space injects into the rank-two quotient and hence is isometric onto it. Commuting local flow fields and metric compatibility give the determinant-area derivative; integrate first on a finite slab before epsilon differentiation, justified by joint C1 regularity and compact C. B0=0 fixes the background density. The affine future boundary fixes the sign of the stress tail. Continuity on a compact initial slab plus the absolute first-moment bound controls the transverse unweighted tail even at lambda0; Tonelli on its absolute value then justifies Fubini and the finite area limit. Zero stress yields constant varied area; signed stress need not yield positive area difference. No entropy or modular identification, NEC, empirical inference, choice selection or converse is used. Wall §2.2 and Reall §§4.6/4.8 are source context; the argument is locally explicit.
